arxiv-2106-02633.title: A Novel Test of Quasar Orientation Journal: ApJL
arxiv-2106-02633.creator: Gordon T. Richards, Richard M. Plotkin, Paul C. Hewett, Amy L. Rankine, Angelica B. Rivera, Yue Shen, Ohad Shemmer
arxiv-2106-02633.description: Abstract The orientation of the disk of material accreting onto supermassive black holes that power quasars is one of most important quantities that are needed to understand quasars—both individually and in the ensemble average. We present a hypothesis for determining comparatively edge-on orientation in a subset of quasars (both radio loud and radio quiet).

arxiv-2201-00059.title: iCaps: Iterative Category-level Object Pose and Shape Estimation
arxiv-2201-00059.creator: Xinke Deng, Junyi Geng, Timothy Bretl, Yu Xiang, Dieter Fox
arxiv-2201-00059.description: Abstract This paper proposes a category-level 6D object pose and shape estimation approach iCaps 1 1 1 The code is at http://github.com/aerogjy/iCaps . A video can be found at https://youtu.be/3AMcM3uUaUw . , which allows tracking 6D poses of unseen objects in a category and estimating their 3D shapes.

arxiv-2310-17625.title: The metallicity dependence and evolutionary times of merging binary black holes: Combined constraints from individual gravitational-wave detections and the stochastic background
arxiv-2310-17625.creator: Kevin Turbang, Max Lalleman, Thomas A. Callister, Nick van Remortel
arxiv-2310-17625.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kevin Turbang, Max Lalleman, Thomas A. Callister, Nick van Remortel. The advent of gravitational-wave astronomy is now allowing for the study of compact binary merger demographics throughout the Universe. This information can be leveraged as tools for understanding massive stars, their environments, and their evolution. One active question is the nature of compact binary formation: the environmental and chemical conditions required for black hole birth and the time delays experienced by binaries before they merge.

arxiv-2405-00884.title: What’s So Hard about the Monty Hall Problem?
arxiv-2405-00884.creator: Rafael C. Alvarado
arxiv-2405-00884.description: Abstract The Monty Hall problem is notorious for its deceptive simplicity. Although today it is widely used as a provocative thought experiment to introduce Bayesian thinking to students of probability, in the not so distant past it was rejected by established mathematicians.

arxiv-2506-02660.title: Tarallo: Evading Behavioral Malware Detectors in the Problem Space
arxiv-2506-02660.creator: Gabriele Digregorio, Salvatore Maccarrone, Mario D’Onghia, Luigi Gallo, Michele Carminati, Mario Polino, Stefano Zanero
arxiv-2506-02660.description: Abstract Machine learning algorithms can effectively classify malware through dynamic behavior but are susceptible to adversarial attacks . Existing attacks, however, often fail to find an effective solution in both the feature and problem spaces. This issue arises from not addressing the intrinsic nondeterministic nature of malware, namely executing the same sample multiple times may yield significantly different behaviors.

arxiv-2507-04160.title: HyperSumm-RL: A Dialogue Summarization Framework for Modeling Leadership Perception in Social Robots DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: In Proceedings of the 36th ACM Conference on Hypertext and Social Media; September 15–19, 2025; Chicago, IL ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Computing methodologies
arxiv-2507-04160.creator: Subasish Das
arxiv-2507-04160.description: Abstract . This paper introduces HyperSumm-RL, a hypertext-aware summarization and interaction analysis framework designed to investigate human perceptions of social robot leadership through long-form dialogue. The system utilizes a structured Natural Language Processing (NLP) workflow that combines transformer-based long dialogue summarization, leadership style modeling, and user response analysis, enabling scalable evaluation of social robots in complex human-robot interaction (HRI) settings.

arxiv-2511-09009.title: Stability, electronic disruption, and anisotropic superconductivity of hydrogenated trilayer metal tetraborides (MB 4 H; M=Be, Mg, Ca, Al)
arxiv-2511-09009.creator: Jakkapat Seeyangnok, Udomsilp Pinsook*, Graeme J. Ackland
arxiv-2511-09009.description: Abstract The discovery of superconductivity in MgB 2 ( T c = 39 T_{c}=39 K) 42 established metal diborides (MB 2 ) as a promising class of conventional superconductors. Recent advances in fabrication techniques have enabled the synthesis of 2D MgB 2 with a T c T_{c} of 36 K 3 , reigniting interest in layered metal borides.

arxiv-2602-07563.title: Moment generating functions in combinatorial optimization: Bipartite matching
arxiv-2602-07563.creator: Johan Wästlund
arxiv-2602-07563.description: Abstract In a random model of minimum cost bipartite matching based on exponentially distributed edge costs, we show that the distribution of the cost of the optimal solution can be computed efficiently. The distribution is represented by its moment generating function, which in this model is always a rational function.

britannica-1911-saint-arnaud-jacques-ler.title: Saint Arnaud, Jacques Leroy de (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-saint-arnaud-jacques-ler.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-saint-arnaud-jacques-ler.description: Article 'Saint Arnaud, Jacques Leroy de' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. of France, was born at Paris on the 20th of August 1801. He entered the army in 1817, and after ten years of garrison service, which he varied by gambling and wild courses, he still held only the lowest commissioned grade. He then resigned, led a life of adventure in several lands and returned to the army at thirty as a sub-lieutenant.

europmc-pmc4875063.title: Rate of force development: physiological and methodological considerations.
europmc-pmc4875063.creator: Maffiuletti NA, Aagaard P, Blazevich AJ, Folland J, Tillin N, Duchateau J.
europmc-pmc4875063.description: The evaluation of rate of force development during rapid contractions has recently become quite popular for characterising explosive strength of athletes, elderly individuals and patients. The main aims of this narrative review are to describe the neuromuscular determinants of...

plos-pone-0010619.title: An Environment-Sensitive Synthetic Microbial Ecosystem
plos-pone-0010619.creator: Bo Hu, Jin Du, Rui-yang Zou et al.
plos-pone-0010619.description: PLOS ONE research article. Microbial ecosystems have been widely used in industrial production, but the inter-relationships of organisms within them haven't been completely clarified due to complex composition and structure of natural microbial ecosystems. So it is challenging for ecologists to get deep in

pmc-10598061.title: Proteomic characterization of aging-driven changes in the mouse brain by co-expression network analysis
pmc-10598061.creator: Kazuya Tsumagari, Yoshiaki Sato, Hirofumi Aoyagi, Hideyuki Okano, Junro Kuromitsu
pmc-10598061.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Brain aging causes a progressive decline in functional capacity and is a strong risk factor for dementias such as Alzheimer’s disease. To characterize age-related proteomic changes in the brain, we used quantitative proteomics to examine brain tissues, cortex and hippocampus, of mice at three age points (3, 15, and 24 months old), and quantified more than 7000 proteins in total with high reproducibility.

pmc-10747478.title: An Error Estimation System for Close-Range Photogrammetric Systems and Algorithms †
pmc-10747478.creator: Anton Poroykov, Olga Pechinskaya, Ekaterina Shmatko, Danil Eremin, Nikita Sivov
pmc-10747478.description: Close-range photogrammetry methods are widely used for non-contact and accurate measurements of surface shapes. These methods are based on calculating the three-dimensional coordinates of an object from two-dimensional images using special digital processing algorithms. Due to the relatively complex measurement principle, the accurate estimation of the photogrammetric measurement error is a non-trivial task.

pmc-11508388.title: The Role of Natriuretic Peptides in the Management of Heart Failure with a Focus on the Patient with Diabetes
pmc-11508388.creator: Michela Vergani, Rosa Cannistraci, Gianluca Perseghin, Stefano Ciardullo, Ioannis Vogiatzis
pmc-11508388.description: Natriuretic peptides (NPs) are polypeptide hormones involved in the homeostasis of the cardiovascular system. They are produced by cardiomyocytes and regulate circulating blood volume and sodium concentration. Clinically, measurements of brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP) are recommended by international guidelines as evidence is accumulating on their usefulness.

pmc-11693301.title: SENSOR-BASED MONITORING OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY IN OLDER ADULTS SIX MONTHS POST-FALL: MODERATING FACTORS
pmc-11693301.creator: Laura Schmidt, Tim Stuckenschneider, Robert Kwiecien, Tania Zieschang
pmc-11693301.description: Older individuals who have experienced a fall often experience concerns about falling, impaired activities of daily living, and reduced physical activity (PA). Changes in PA following a fall are often influenced by moderators such as age or fall history; however, these moderators remain understudied.

pmc-12436770.title: Mosè Barabba: A case study between forensic and cultural psychiatry
pmc-12436770.creator: J. Santambrogio, Antonino Giancontieri, Elisabetta Leon, Elena Miragliotta, Enrico Capuzzi, Fabrizia Colmegna, Massimo Clerici
pmc-12436770.description: The presentation gives a narrative account of a case of ethnopsychiatry and criminology from the standpoint of the care network, with personal details supplied by the patient himself. The person involved, Mosè Barabba, was born in Sierra Leone where he was kidnapped and forced to become a child soldier at a very early age.

pmc-12534601.title: Chronic 40 Hz light flicker mitigates epileptogenesis through a visual pathway associated with the dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus shell
pmc-12534601.creator: Lei Wang, Wenhao Xu, Kai Wang, Jinwei Yang, Hanli Li, Qi Wang, Zhong Dong, Xiaoyu Zhang, Qian Meng, Fengqing Lu, Jianxiang Lei, Yujing Yang, Kai Wang, Lijie Feng, Yu Wang
pmc-12534601.description: Altered gamma activity is associated with epilepsy. Gamma entrainment using sensory stimuli (GENUS), a non-invasive, exogenous stimulation by rhythmic 40 Hz light flicker, strengthens gamma activity in the primary visual cortex (V1) and suppresses spike generation. Here, we assessed the effect of GENUS on epileptogenesis in male mice with status epilepticus induced by pilocarpine.

pmc-12631445.title: Clarifying species boundaries between bocachico (Prochilodus magdalenae) and bocachico de Maracaibo (Prochilodus reticulatus) (characiformes: Prochilodontidae) using complete mitochondrial genomes
pmc-12631445.creator: Jonny Yepes-Blandón, Diego Almansa-Villa, María José Benítez-Galeano, Daiana Mir, Jim Hernández-Rangel, Víctor Atencio-García, Ana Estrada-Posada, Nélida Rodríguez-Osorio
pmc-12631445.description: The accurate phylogenetic distinction between Prochilodus magdalenae and Prochilodus reticulatus (Characiformes: Prochilodontidae) has been hindered by overlapping morphology and limited sequence data. Previous studies, relying on partial mitochondrial markers, have even suggested that Prochilodus magdalenae and Prochilodus reticulatus might be a single species. This study presents three annotated complete mitochondrial genomes for P.

pmc-12642191.title: Efficacy of cognitive and behavioral therapy (CBT) treatment for individuals living with symptoms associated with environmental factors (SAEF): protocol for a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12642191.creator: Victor Pitron, Tara Petzke, Ingrid Zablith, Marion Revillot-Tirot, Clémence Forestier-Dupuch, Fatima Zohra Ibouchna, Michael Witthöft, Damien Léger, Lynda Bensefa-Colas, Omer Van den Bergh, Cédric Lemogne
pmc-12642191.description: BackgroundTreatment for symptoms associated with environmental factors (SAEF), such as electrohypersensitivity or multiple chemical sensitivity, have been sparsely investigated thus far.MethodsIn this parallel, two-armed open-label randomized controlled trial, we will apply a treatment model for SAEF based on cognitive behavioral therapy.

pmc-13053730.title: Bacterial cellulose–enhanced MTA versus conventional MTA for indirect pulp capping in primary teeth: a randomized controlled clinical trial
pmc-13053730.creator: V. Lalitha Priya, Kavitha Ramar
pmc-13053730.description: This randomized controlled trial aimed to compare the clinical and radiographic success rates of bacterial cellulose-reinforced MTA (BC-MTA) and conventional MTA in indirect pulp capping (IPT) treatment of primary teeth. A total of 40 primary molars diagnosed for IPT were randomly allocated into two groups: Group I (BC-MTA, n = 20) and Group II (Conventional MTA, n = 20).

pmc-13087582.title: Comprehensive evaluation of sacchachitosan-based transdermal films for wound care: Physical, chemical, and biological parameters
pmc-13087582.creator: Sneha Paul, C. Sheela Sasikumar
pmc-13087582.description: In the present investigation, the development and comparative assessment of sacchachitosan-based transdermal films loaded with biosynthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) for wound-healing applications were reported. Sacchachitosan, a fungal chitosan obtained from Ganoderma lucidum, was mixed with gelatin and glycerol to improve film flexibility, bio-adhesiveness, and moisture retention.

pmc-13094924.title: The effect of human genital warts virus on the quality of women’s sexual life: A look at the effective factors
pmc-13094924.creator: Hajar Habibpour, Shabnam Omidvar, Afsaneh Bakhtiari, Karimollah Hajian-Tilaki, Hossein Ghorbani
pmc-13094924.description: BACKGROUND:The global prevalence of HPV is rising. Despite numerous studies on its effects on psychological dimensions, quality of life, and sexual performance, its impact on women’s sexual quality of life (QoL) remains unclear. This study assesses the sexual QoL among women with genital HPV and the influencing factors.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cross-sectional study was conducted on 395 women undergoing HPV testing.

pmc-13333931.title: 18F‐PSMA‐1007 PET/CT Demonstrates Higher Accuracy for Biochemically Recurrent Prostate Cancer Compared to Contemporary Conventional Imaging
pmc-13333931.creator: Zachary Stanton, Bonnie Woloschuk, Alexander Tamm, Ryan Hung, Adwait Trivedi, Michael Kolinsky, Nawaid Usmani, Lindsay Rowe, Ronald Moore, Frank Wuest, Jonathan Abele
pmc-13333931.description: PurposeThe goal of this study was to compare the accuracy of 18F‐PSMA‐1007 PET/CT to contemporary conventional imaging (contrast‐enhanced CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis and a 99mTc‐MDP whole body bone scan with SPECT/CT of the torso) in the setting of biochemically recurrent prostate cancer.

pmc-13556558.title: 511. Multimodal AI for depression detection: integrating facial expressions and semantic analysis in outpatient care
pmc-13556558.creator: M-F Lin, Sp Konara mudiyanselage, H-H Tseng
pmc-13556558.description: BackgroundDepression remains underdetected in outpatient settings due to reliance on self-report measures, stigma, and time constraints in routine clinical care. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) enable objective, scalable approaches for identifying depressive symptoms using behavioral and linguistic markers. However, evidence for the clinical utility of multimodal AI systems in real-world outpatient populations remains limited.

pmc-13577010.title: Antibiotic hybrids: A promising strategy to replenish the pipeline and combat antimicrobial resistance
pmc-13577010.creator: Yeongseo Lee, Yeo Jin Kim, Minhee Oh, Joon-Ho Lee, Saemee Song, Jaesung Kwak
pmc-13577010.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses an ongoing threat to global health, with the number of deaths directly attributable to AMR projected to rise to 8 million. One of the main reasons for the current crisis is the depletion of antibiotic candidates in clinical pipelines. To address this, more preclinical candidates must be advanced into development.

uslaw-usc-t15-s7711.description: United States Code, Title 15 (Commerce And Trade); Chapter 103 (Controlling The Assault Of Non-Solicited Pornography And Marketing). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general The Commission may issue regulations to implement the provisions of this Act (not including the amendments made by sections 4 and 12). Any such regulations shall be issued in accordance with section 553 of title 5.
